title: Units and Measurements

standard_text: The international system of units; measurement of length, mass and time; accuracy and precision of instruments; errors in measurement; significant figures; dimensions of physical quantities, dimensional formulae and dimensional analysis and its applications.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 1 Units and Measurements: SI units, prefixes, significant figures, errors, unit conversion and dimensional analysis. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Every measurement = number × unit, with an error.
key_sub: Check formulae with dimensions [M L T].
body_html:
How to think about it

SI has seven base units: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela; all others are derived. Every measurement has an uncertainty: random errors fall when we average many readings, systematic errors (such as a zero error) do not. Significant figures show how precisely a value is known.

Relative errors add when quantities are multiplied or divided, and multiply by n for a power n. Dimensions write a quantity in terms of M, L and T: force is [M L T⁻²]. A formula must have the same dimensions on both sides, but dimensions cannot find pure numbers like 2π.

Example

Significant figures in 0.02040?

leading zeros do not count

2, 0, 4, 0

Answer: 4

Example

% error in V = r³ if r has 1% error?

3 × 1%

Answer: 3%

Common mistakes

  • Counting leading zeros as significant.
  • Adding absolute errors instead of relative errors in a product.
  • Thinking dimensional analysis proves a formula right.

faq.q: What are the seven SI base units?
faq.a: Metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela.

faq.q: How do errors combine in a product?
faq.a: The relative (percentage) errors add: if Z = AB, ΔZ/Z = ΔA/A + ΔB/B.

items.q: The radius of a sphere is measured with an error of 2%. What is the percentage error in its volume (V = 4πr³/3)?
items.e: For V ∝ r³ the relative error is multiplied by 3: 3 × 2% = 6%.

items.q: The radius of a sphere is measured with an error of 0.5%. What is the percentage error in its volume (V = 4πr³/3)?
